note: Curated taxonomy derived from the 250-block sample (Phase 2). Raw labels in methodology/labels/ are left as observed; aliases map raw names to canonical ones. Edit this file to change the taxonomy, then run `npm run labels`.

hero.title: Hero
hero.definition: The above-the-fold impression: a large specimen of the family, the tagline, and a call to action that sets the tone.

story.title: Story
story.definition: Where the family came from and where it is going: the brief, the references, the decisions that shaped it, in the maker’s own voice.

glyph-table.title: Glyph table
glyph-table.definition: Every glyph in the font, rendered from the font file, and the scripts and languages it covers.

type-tester.title: Type tester
type-tester.definition: Interactive controls a visitor can drive: axis sliders, an editable text field, feature toggles; at the extreme, the whole site as a tool or game.

specimen-showcase.title: Specimen showcase
specimen-showcase.definition: The family shown in real use and in display compositions, from waterfalls to prop collages to editorial walls, plus overviews of the styles.

design-details.title: Design details
design-details.definition: The micro-decisions behind the drawing: spacing, alternates, OpenType features, true italics, optical sizes, and comparisons that make them visible.

checkout.title: Checkout
checkout.definition: Acquiring the font: pricing, formats, licences, trials or free downloads, and the copy and social proof that convert.

footer.title: Footer
footer.definition: Colophon, contact and legal: the credibility line and the last thing visitors read, plus the site furniture around the specimen.

hero.definition: The above-the-fold first impression: what the visitor sees before scrolling.

giant-wordmark.definition: The family name set as large as the viewport allows on a flat field, little else; may mix styles letter by letter to show range.
giant-wordmark.cues: one dominant name, flat colour, minimal copy

sentence-as-specimen.definition: A headline sentence about the font, set in the font (sometimes beside one oversized glyph or rotating through styles): the pitch is the specimen.
sentence-as-specimen.cues: readable claim or announcement in display size, CTA nearby

typeset-page.definition: A classical typeset composition (title page, broadside, dictionary entry) that uses the family's own hierarchy, italics and ornaments.
typeset-page.cues: centred stacks, rules, ornaments, multiple sizes and italics

kinetic-type.definition: The type in motion is the hero: animated, 3D, generative, video clips, or axes driven by scroll.
kinetic-type.cues: canvas/video/WebGL, scroll-scrubbed variation, the capture looks mid-animation

interactive-specimen.definition: The hero is a specimen the visitor manipulates straight away (axes, weight, contrast, text), via controls or the wheel.
interactive-specimen.cues: sliders, toggles or editable text inside the first screen

construction-drawing.definition: A glyph shown as its construction (Bézier points, skeleton, strokes), often drawn on.
construction-drawing.cues: outline points, handles, metric lines in the hero

name-over-photo.definition: Name and a short line over a full-bleed mood photograph.
name-over-photo.cues: landscape or scene photo, type overlaid

material-photo.definition: A photograph of physical material (paper, textile, objects) carrying or framing the type.
material-photo.cues: tactile still life, the type printed or knitted on the material

illustration-scene.definition: An illustrated scene or mascot staged with the type; the illustration sets the tone.

prop-collage.definition: A collage of designed artefacts (documents, tickets, packaging, diagrams) set in the font, implying a fictional world.
prop-collage.cues: many small designed objects, all set in the font

product-landing.definition: The software-product landing pattern: headline, tagline, paragraph, primary and secondary buttons.
product-landing.cues: SaaS layout, 'Try it now' and 'GitHub' buttons, common for coding fonts

mini-game.definition: The hero is a small playable game built from the page's own elements (e.g. Pong); collisions or score change the name's axes, CTAs can be game pieces.
mini-game.cues: ball, paddles, score in the first screen

click-to-stamp.definition: An almost empty first screen; each click drops a word or phrase in the font at the pointer with randomised style or axis values, so the visitor composes the hero.

strip-mixer.definition: A typeset page cut into headline, deck and body strips, each its own carousel of styles cycling on its own timer and swipeable, so the page keeps recombining.

glyph-grid-sampler.definition: A small name over a large grid of characters from every covered script, often on writing-practice guide cells.
glyph-grid-sampler.cues: grid of CJK/Latin characters in guide cells

intro-animation.definition: A timed or pinned full-screen sequence played before the page proper, like film opening titles.

title-sequence.definition: Full-screen frames revealing name, facts and specimen in sequence, often skippable.

story.definition: Where the family comes from and why: brief, references, process, people.

origin-reference.definition: The source or inspiration (historical artefact, technology, place, genre history) explained in prose and shown visually.

essay.definition: Long-form first-person or editorial text (designer essay, process chapters, commissioner's foreword), laid out like an article.

making-of.definition: The process shown visually: sketches, proofs, iterations, photos of the designer at work.
making-of.cues: process images with little text, stages

design-brief.definition: The problem the font solves (purpose, readers, constraints, principles) stated as a list or spec.

large-text-intro.definition: A short 'about' paragraph set large in the font, so the description doubles as a text specimen.
large-text-intro.cues: one big paragraph near the top

article-teaser.definition: A short teaser and a link to an off-page article or interview about the making.

scroll-narrative.definition: A pinned, scroll-driven sequence telling a concept metaphor through animated type and diagrams.

self-test-evidence.definition: The design rationale backed by a small test the visitor runs on themselves (reading speed, legibility).
self-test-evidence.cues: a quiz or timer next to research prose

designer-bio.definition: A short, informal bio of the designer with contact links.

info-popover.definition: Section copy hidden behind a small info button and shown as a popover beside the specimen; the page shows type first, text on demand.

expandable-timeline.definition: A dated timeline of rows that expand into text cards on hover or click, with the year and title switching from light to heavy weight.
expandable-timeline.cues: years in a column, accordion rows

faq.definition: Practical questions and answers about the font, as a collapsed accordion (often grouped by tabs) or an open anchored list.

glyph-table.definition: The character set itself, all or by category.

full-grid.definition: The whole character set in uniform cells, in encoding order (sometimes with key labels for dingbat fonts).

glyph-inspector.definition: A grid plus a large preview of the selected or hovered glyph on its metric lines.
glyph-inspector.cues: big glyph panel, cap-height and x-height lines

category-lines.definition: The set typeset as running lines per category (or one moving line), no cells.
category-lines.cues: A–Z, a–z, 0–9 as lines of text

category-tabs.definition: Tabs or a dropdown switch a large-size strip of one category at a time.

bento-cards.definition: A grid of cards, each a slice of the set or one feature (arrows, numerals, ligatures).

keymap-grid.definition: Pictogram or dingbat cells labelled with the key that types them.
keymap-grid.cues: key letter in each cell corner

type-tester.definition: Interactive: the visitor types and/or drives size, axes and features.

per-row-controls.definition: Several sample rows, each with its own style, size and leading controls.
per-row-controls.cues: a control strip on every row

global-toolbar.definition: One persistent toolbar restyles all editable samples on the page.
global-toolbar.cues: sticky bar of selects and sliders

labelled-editable-lines.definition: Each style gets a small label and editable lines at a fitting size; click to type, no toolbar.
labelled-editable-lines.cues: contenteditable lines, style labels, no controls

slider-sandbox.definition: One editable sample with a few axis and size sliders around it.

feature-toggle-board.definition: One big sample line plus a panel of OpenType feature toggles labelled with their tags.

in-context-editable.definition: A realistic layout (classifieds, menu, poster) whose text is editable.
in-context-editable.cues: editable text inside a designed artefact

code-playground.definition: A mock code editor with language tabs and themes, set in the (coding) font, with font controls.

creative-toy.definition: A playful maker that turns the font into a composition: patterns, shareable images, style pairings, word-by-word styling.
creative-toy.cues: share or download buttons, presets, unusual gestures

auto-fit-editable-lines.definition: Editable display lines that rescale to fill the column width as you type; no size or axis controls, at most a style switch for the stack.

pointer-xy-axes.definition: The pointer's x and y position (or device tilt) each drive one variable axis, with edge tracks or labels showing live values; no sliders to grab.
pointer-xy-axes.cues: axis labels at the edges, moves with the cursor

mockup-generator.definition: A short text field (with style and colour pickers) whose input is rendered into a wall of realistic scenes (billboards, gadgets, screens), so visitors see their words in use.
mockup-generator.cues: input field above a grid of mockups

palette-editor.definition: One editable sample in a colour font with a colour picker per palette layer (outline, fill, gradient stops, randomise) that rewrites the palette live.
palette-editor.cues: colour swatches beside a colour-font sample

write-on-playback.definition: Editable samples in a font with a time (write-on) axis: a play button draws the text stroke by stroke and a timeline slider scrubs it.

xy-pad.definition: One editable sample beside a 2D pad: dragging one handle sets two axes at once (e.g. weight × optical size).
xy-pad.cues: square pad with a crosshair handle

outline-editor.definition: The visitor drags a glyph's outline points and Bézier handles, with undo/redo, reset and image download.
outline-editor.cues: points and handles on a big glyph

sound-reactive-axis.definition: The microphone level drives an axis (e.g. weight) of a large word, letter by letter.
sound-reactive-axis.cues: microphone permission, letters pulsing with sound

specimen-showcase.definition: The family shown in use or in display compositions.

word-stack.definition: Display words or phrases stacked vertically, often cropped, for rhythm and character.

in-use-mockups.definition: Realistic applications (posters, books, screens, signage, client work) as a wall, carousel, shuffler or filmed object.

prop-collage.definition: Invented artefacts (UI windows, tickets, files, stickers) set in the font, collaged into a scene.

poster-series.definition: A sequence of self-contained poster or specimen-page compositions, often pastiching a period.
poster-series.cues: full-width graphic panels one after another

editorial-in-use.definition: The font running a real or realistic publication (articles, magazine pages) with genuine content.

kinetic-scenes.definition: Animated, generative or physics compositions (falling or scattered glyphs, liquid) after the hero.

use-case-samples.definition: Tabs or panels with realistic content samples per use case (code, data tables, UI).

modular-grid.definition: A uniform grid of cells mixing large glyphs, sentences and notes, like a specimen sheet.

themed-infographic.definition: An interactive infographic on the font's theme, set in the font so the numerals and labels do real work.

generative-layout-stream.definition: An endless scroll appending randomly composed layout modules (columns, captions, lists, display words) with themed, often editable copy.

slider-morph-mockups.definition: Realistic layouts (ads, tickets, flyers) each with an axis slider that morphs the whole design between the axis extremes.

size-waterfall.definition: The same running text at a descending series of labelled sizes, from display to caption, often in several weights side by side; sometimes a light/dark switch.

family-overview.definition: The family's styles and structure at a glance.

style-word-grid.definition: Every style named and shown on a sample word or the same paragraph.
style-word-grid.cues: style labels plus samples in a grid or stack

designspace-map.definition: The family laid out along its axes: a matrix, a cube, or clickable stops that set the sample.
designspace-map.cues: width × weight table, axis cube, stop pickers

big-number-stats.definition: The family's size stated as huge figures (glyphs, weights, styles).

design-details.definition: The micro-decisions: features, alternates, axes, spacing, construction.

feature-before-after.definition: A feature or alternate shown off vs on (side by side, overlaid, toggled or typed in a loop) with a short explanation.

feature-index.definition: Every stylistic set or ligature group catalogued as cards or tiles (input → output), often toggleable or exportable as settings.

axis-explainer.definition: Each variable axis demonstrated on its own: a word plus slider, labelled steps, or animation fitting frames.
axis-explainer.cues: axis names, steps, one axis at a time

annotated-specimen.definition: Letterforms with technical annotations or numbered figures (measurements, ink traps, angles), one decision per row.

system-diagrams.definition: The family's logic (weight curve, optical sizes, widths) explained with charts, like a design-system manual.

design-notes.definition: A sequence of design decisions, each with a visual and a short caption, as a carousel or video tiles.
design-notes.cues: slides or looping tiles per topic

highlighted-in-context.definition: Ligatures, alternates or special glyphs set inside a display sentence and picked out in an accent colour, discovered in context rather than in a catalogue.

hover-css-inspector.definition: A page-wide inspector: hovering any sample shows a crosshair and a tooltip with that text's CSS (size, leading, weight, features).

multiscript-specimen.definition: Sample lines in several scripts, each tagged with script and settings.

diacritic-word-wall.definition: Real words from many languages chosen for their diacritics, at display size.

coverage-statement.definition: A big-type sentence stating the coverage instead of showing it.

script-catalogue.definition: Each supported script named in its own script at display size, in a grid, with style counts and notes on how it was made.

language-name-list.definition: The supported languages listed by name, as small running text, columns, or a per-script table with credits and style counts; the list is the proof.
language-name-list.cues: long alphabetical list of language names

language-profile.definition: A deep dive into the one language the family was designed for: special characters with Unicode and keyboard notes, a map, the alphabet and a sample text.

translated-word-picker.definition: A wheel or list of language names beside one giant word; picking a language swaps the word for its translation.

comparison.definition: This font set against others or against previous versions.

versus-tabs.definition: Tabs pick a rival typeface; the same text is set in both, stacked.

pointer-wipe.definition: Two typefaces or versions on the same sample, compared by a divider that follows the pointer (clip-path wipe) or by one pointer pad driving both.

reference-morph.definition: A custom variable font interpolates a reference typeface (generic or historical model) into this one; scroll or a loop scrubs the morph between two labelled ends.
reference-morph.cues: two labels at the ends, shapes morphing

source-reset.definition: A scan of a historical source (ad, specimen, cover) followed by the same text reset in the new typeface at the same scale.
source-reset.cues: scan, then the same layout set fresh

lineage-lineup.definition: One letter from each historical model leading to the new typeface, lined up on a timeline with source, date and role: a typographic family tree.
lineage-lineup.cues: row of the same letter across eras

quote-columns.definition: User quotes set in the font, in plain columns.

embedded-social-posts.definition: Embedded posts from users, with avatars and handles.

award-logo-strip.definition: A single row of award, prize or press logos as social proof, no quotes.
award-logo-strip.cues: logo row, often under the hero

checkout.definition: How the visitor acquires the font: purchase, trial or free download.

on-page-cart.definition: Buying happens on the page: licence picker, packages and prices, preview, add to cart.

link-out-cta.definition: Prominent buy, trial or download buttons linking to an external shop or repository.

free-download.definition: A free download with a plain-language licence summary and/or developer install instructions.
free-download.cues: OFL, npm or brew commands, press kit

build-configurator.definition: Options (alternates, spacing, ligatures) select which pre-built files you download.
build-configurator.cues: option toggles plus a download button

package-price-sheet.definition: The licence packages (family, subfamily, single style) laid out with contents and ‘from’ prices, illustrated with style samples; the purchase itself happens in an external shop.
package-price-sheet.cues: package cards with prices, buy links out

supporter-tier-wall.definition: For a free font: donation tiers shown as medals with amounts, each followed by the names of supporters at that level; the thank-you wall is also the ask.

footer.definition: The end of the page: colophon, contact, legal.

credits-colophon.definition: Credits: designers, contributors, testers, tools, fonts used.

big-sign-off.definition: A large closing statement, then small legal lines.

personal-sign-off.definition: An informal closing note from the designer.

slim-legal-bar.definition: One or two lines: copyright and credit.

navigation.definition: Wayfinding and cross-promotion beyond the global nav.

related-projects.definition: Cards linking to the designer's or foundry's other fonts.

scroll-spy-nav.definition: A fixed bar or tab strip of the page's chapters that marks the current one while scrolling (highlight, needle on a dial); click to jump.

toc-drawer.definition: An off-canvas panel of section links opened from a fixed edge tab or menu icon.

next-chapter-link.definition: A band at the end of a page linking to the next numbered page of a multi-page microsite.

playground-app.definition: The whole site is an application rather than a scrolling page.

keyboard-driven-app.definition: A single-screen app driven by keyboard shortcuts.

desktop-os-windows.definition: The site staged as a desktop OS with draggable windows.

configurator-wizard.definition: A one-screen app where numbered steps build the visitor's own version of the font (axes, alternates, weights, name) with a live preview, saved as a shareable ID and ending in trial or purchase.
configurator-wizard.cues: numbered steps, big preview, share/buy at the end

game.definition: A playable game made with the font.

arcade-game.definition: A playable arcade game set in or made from the font (platformer, Pong, Arkanoid), often with a leaderboard and font prizes.

destructible-page.definition: A hidden game layer over the specimen itself: elements can be shot or destroyed with clicks, with sounds, score, unlockable modes and a restore screen.

interlude.definition: Pure transition between sections; no information.

chapter-title-overlay.definition: A fixed full-screen overlay flashing the chapter number or name in giant type each time a chapter scrolls in, then fading.

full-bleed-image.definition: A full-viewport image without text (close-up of the source or of the letters) as a pause between chapters.

scroll-scrubbed-sequence.definition: A pinned, scroll-scrubbed animation (pre-rendered frame sequence or illustration, e.g. doors opening, an object turning or releasing letters) between sections, with little or no text.
scroll-scrubbed-sequence.cues: sticky stage, image changes with scroll

annotated-spacer.definition: Empty bands of the page's visible grid between sections, each labelled with a technical note.
annotated-spacer.cues: grid cells with small labels, no content

ghost-marquee.definition: One sentence from nearby copy, set near viewport height in a very pale tint, scrolling sideways as an endless band between sections.

chrome.definition: Site furniture that is not specimen content (banners, nav).

announcement-banner.definition: A thin site-wide banner (donation, launch, sale).

masthead-nav.definition: A slim header with name, tagline and section tabs, standing in for a hero.

nav-bar.definition: A persistent site bar (top or bottom, fixed or static): name or logo, section links or view tabs, a buy/get button, sometimes toggles such as colour themes.
nav-bar.cues: thin bar, repeated across stitched screens when fixed

scroll-progress-indicator.definition: A sticky element showing scroll progress (bar, dot on a chart, counter).

fragment.definition: Not a component instance: bad cut, empty capture or duplicate. Excluded from pattern counts.

hero/style-medley-wordmark.why: a wordmark; the style mix is an attribute

hero/pitch-beside-glyph.why: the pitch set in the font is the mechanism; the glyph is decoration

hero/title-page.why: renamed to cover broadsides and dictionary entries too

hero/scroll-driven-axes.why: motion is the mechanism; scroll is the driver (ux attribute)

hero/video-mosaic.why: type in motion, delivered as video tiles

story/foreword.why: an essay in the commissioner's voice

specimen-showcase/shuffle-mockup.why: mockups presented one at a time

specimen-showcase/in-use-carousel.why: real client work in a carousel

specimen-showcase/multiscript-lines.why: its purpose is showing script coverage

family-overview/text-block-per-style.why: styles plus samples; a paragraph instead of a word

family-overview/axis-matrix.why: family laid out along its axes

family-overview/instance-picker.why: family laid out along its axes, clickable

design-details/feature-config-builder.why: a catalogue plus export of settings

section-divider/scroll-door-animation.why: type renamed; variant generalised in Phase 3

language-support/coverage-table.why: Phase 3: a tabular form of the language list
